summary: Verify nous V4 atlas-fix audit on the live Plexis v5 grid + design exact, validated fix recipes

result.problems: e1 embedding leak; od_throughput probe-target leak; vis-retail footfall collinear 0.857; hex9 lacks 3 inputs; scale invented vs URA
result.corrected_recipe: new retail-rent layer; relabel occ source; decollinearize composite; hex9 inherit; embedding exclude guard
result.final_acceptance: spread 8x; Orchard>Tampines>Woodlands; URA sign matches; 471 NaN; no rent_retail in meta; occ-cost unchanged

result.problems:
The recipe directionally fixes the audit (it kills the dead-PORT-beats-NASSIM inversion and reproduces the headline numbers — I confirmed coverage 90.2% (471/522), Spearman(new, vis_exit)=+0.434 all / +0.459 scorable, Toa Payoh Central 99, Tampines West 96, Jurong West Central 98, Sengkang Town Centre 98, City Hall 91, dead PORT 41->33, NASSIM 12->75, top-15 all genuine HDB/regional centres). But it has FOUR real problems the acceptance check does not catch:

(1) EMBEDDING TARGET LEAKAGE — the showstopper. retail_footfall_score IS currently an e1 embedding INPUT (verified: it survives EXCLUDE_EXACT/EXCLUDE_PREFIX in embedding/prep_features.py, one of 778 input cols). od_throughput is explicitly EXCLUDED from the embedding because it is the e1 PROBE TARGET. The recipe puts od_throughput in as a literal 0.25-weight term, making the NEW score correlate +0.892 with od_throughput. That injects the probe target straight into the embedding input -> inflated, dishonest e1 probe-recovery. (The OLD score was already +0.891 via dt_pop/iso_*, so the leak pre-exists, but the recipe makes it explicit/direct and trivially detectable.) The memory note project_plexis_e1_embedding states rent/footfall must NOT be embedding inputs — yet on this live grid retail_footfall_score, vis_exit_footfall, dt_pop, iso_walk10_pop, iso_transit15_pop AND rent_resi_psf_med are all embedding inputs today.

(2) NUMERICAL INSTABILITY — pandas .rank(pct=True) defaults to AVERAGE tie handling, so the big zero block gets a NON-zero percentile (dt_pop zero-tie -> 0.199, od -> 0.271, etc.). 413 hexes have ALL FOUR inputs = 0 yet still get blend ~0.20 -> new>0 after rescale. The 'coverage >0' acceptance metric is therefore partly an artifact of tie-averaging, not real activity. Must use method='min' (or subtract the empirical floor).

(3) NA-GATE SIDE EFFECTS — gating zone_type 'unknown' to NaN nukes 247 hexes, 60 of which have real dt_pop>0; across the full gate, 107 hexes currently scored>0 silently become NaN. 'unknown' is genuinely ambiguous, not confirmed non-residential — blanket-NaNing it is more aggressive than the established zone_type NA treatment (which targets confirmed non-residential PAs). Also introducing NaN flips the column to float64; pack_util.save()'s report uses (sub[c]!=0).mean() and NaN!=0 is True, so NaN hexes are mis-counted as nonzero in the pack report (cosmetic bug, not a crash — int(NaN-bearing .min()) is safe because .min() skips NaN).

(4) RESIDUAL COLLINEARITY WITH SIBLINGS / DOUBLE-COUNTING — dt_pop is also the e1 WHO-view driver and iso_*/od_* are FLOW-view; the new score is +0.813 with dt_pop and structurally a re-aggregation of cols already in the master, so it adds no independent signal to the embedding and is pure double-counting if left as an input.
result.corrected_recipe:
In build_retail_pack_sgp.py replace the retail_footfall_score line with a rank-blend, but FIX the four problems:

(1) Drop od_throughput entirely from the blend (it is the e1 probe target). Reweight the remaining three to sum to 1.0. Verified this barely moves anything: NEW(no-od) vs od_throughput falls to +0.84 (carried by iso/dt, unavoidable and acceptable since those are legit master cols), vs vis_exit stays +0.451, and hubs hold (NASSIM 72, Toa Payoh Central 97, Sengkang Town Centre 95).

(2) Use min-tie ranks so genuine all-zero hexes map to 0:
   def rank01(s):
       x = np.log1p(pd.to_numeric(s, errors='coerce').fillna(0).clip(lower=0))
       r = x.rank(pct=True, method='min')   # ties (incl. the zero block) take the MIN rank
       return r
   blend = 0.50*rank01(dt_pop) + 0.30*rank01(iso_walk10_pop) + 0.20*rank01(iso_transit15_pop)
   # daytime presence primary (0.50), walkable catchment (0.30), transit-15 catchment (0.20)

(3) Rescale linearly over observed range, then FORCE all-zero-input hexes to exactly 0:
   new = ((blend - blend.min())/(blend.max()-blend.min())*100).round()
   allzero = (col(df,'dt_pop')<=0)&(col(df,'iso_walk10_pop')<=0)&(col(df,'iso_transit15_pop')<=0)
   new = new.where(~allzero, 0)

(4) NA-gate consistently but DO NOT blanket-gate 'unknown'. Gate only confirmed non-residential:
   gate = df['zone_type'].isin(['nature','islands_restricted','islands_resort','water']) | \
          df['dominant_use'].isin(['open_space','reserve','water'])
   # 'unknown' zone_type: keep scorable but it will self-zero where inputs are 0 (no MRT-exit phantom path remains since vis_exit is gone)
   # dead-cell cleanup: also NA where dominant_use in {transport,utility} AND dt_pop<50 (removes the dead PORT cell honestly)
   gate = gate | (df['dominant_use'].isin(['transport','utility']) & (col(df,'dt_pop')<50))
   o['retail_footfall_score'] = new.where(~gate, np.nan).astype('float32')

(5) MANDATORY embedding-leakage fix (separate file, embedding/prep_features.py): add retail_footfall_score (and the other domain-pack derived *_score cols that re-aggregate master inputs: retail_whitespace_score, format_fit_score, retail_competition_pressure, etc.) plus vis_exit_footfall to EXCLUDE so the score is a derived PRODUCT, never an embedding INPUT. Confirm rent_resi_psf_med / rent_* are also excluded per the project_plexis_e1_embedding policy. Then rebuild the e1 embedding. (This is the actual root-cause fix; without it the score change just shuffles leakage rather than removing it.)

(6) Fix the cosmetic report bug in pack_util.save(): compute nonzero_pct as ((sub[c]!=0)&sub[c].notna()).mean() so NaN-gated hexes are not mis-counted as nonzero.

Do NOT touch format_fit_score's separate vis_exit_footfall use in THIS item, but note for a follow-up audit that format_fit_score is itself an embedding input and also leaks vis_exit/walkability.
result.final_acceptance:
Run on hex/hex8_all_features.parquet AFTER rebuilding the retail pack, folding into master, AND rebuilding the e1 embedding:
(1) Coverage (real, not tie-artifact): with method='min' ranks and all-zero force-to-0, retail_footfall_score>0 for >=80% of the scorable universe (zone_type not in nature/islands*/water and dominant_use not in open_space/reserve/water, and not the transport/utility<50 dead cells). Target ~85-90%; the 413 all-zero-input hexes MUST now score exactly 0 (verify min over all-zero-input hexes == 0).
(2) Collinearity vs the replaced signal: Spearman(retail_footfall_score, vis_exit_footfall) < 0.60 overall AND within scorable. Target ~+0.45.
(3) NO embedding target leakage: after re-running embedding/prep_features.py, assert retail_footfall_score, vis_exit_footfall, format_fit_score, retail_whitespace_score and rent_* are NOT in the input column list; and assert Spearman(any embedding INPUT col, od_throughput) is not driven by a derived footfall score (retail_footfall_score must be absent from inputs). The e1 probe-recovery R2 for od_throughput must NOT increase versus the pre-change baseline (no leakage-inflation).
(4) Hub sanity (od-free blend): Toa Payoh Central >=95, Tampines West >=92, Jurong West Central >=95, Sengkang Town Centre >=92, City Hall >=85, NASSIM >=65, and NASSIM > dead PORT 886520d811fffff (which must be NaN under the transport/dt<50 gate).
(5) Dead-cell: 886520d811fffff is NaN (gated); no transport/utility cell with dt_pop<50 has a positive score.
(6) Top-15 are genuine HDB town centres / regional hubs (Tampines, Toa Payoh, Sengkang, Punggol/Rivervale/Anchorvale, Jurong West, Bedok North, Yishun, Choa Chu Kang) with zero station-only phantoms.
(7) pack report nonzero_pct uses notna-aware count; no NaN-as-nonzero inflation.

result.problems:
The core idea (decouple from lu_business_pct, anchor on physical buildings, gate ring-smear by own presence) is correct and the prototype mechanically reproduces its headline numbers on the live grid. But the recipe is NOT safe to ship as written. Four problems, two serious:

PROBLEM 1 — STALE BASELINE / ALREADY-FIXED COLUMN (process error). The recipe's "before" (corr(score,lu_business_pct)=0.644 vs corr(score,bldg)=0.246, FN bld>=25 = 21, Murai=0.0) NO LONGER EXISTS on the live grid. A prior fix `nous_v4_hex8.py` already ran today (14:31:56, backup at backups/v4fix_20260624_143156) and rewrote industrial_adjacency_score to `norm(0.55*rank01(bldg)+0.30*rank01(pc_cat_industrial_mfg)+0.15*rank01(max1_pc_cat_industrial_mfg))`. I measured the LIVE master (n=1191): corr(score,bldg)=0.552, corr(score,lu_business_pct)=0.371, corr(score,pc_cat_industrial_mfg)=0.550, FN(bld>=25)=0, FN(bld>=40)=0, Murai top cell=0.710. So the false-NEGATIVE half is ALREADY solved on the live grid; the only surviving defect is the heartland false-POSITIVE (211 base / 91 score>=0.5 = 43%, WORSE than the 42 the recipe quotes, because the live rank-blend has no residential dilution). Acceptance condition 4's "false-neg for bld>=25 drops 21->5" is, against the live column, a REGRESSION 0->5, not an improvement. The reviewer's whole 'ordering is inverted' premise is false against current state.

PROBLEM 2 — PETROCHEMICAL / FOOTPRINT-BLIND HAZARD ZONES ZEROED (SERIOUS, breaks a downstream consumer). By fully decoupling from lu_business_pct and anchoring only on bldg_industrial_count / pc_cat_industrial_mfg, the recipe drives 72 footprint-blind heavy-industry cells to ~0: Jurong Island & Bukom (petrochemical refineries), Gul Basin, Pasir Ris Wafer Fab Park, Tuas View Extension, Samulun/Shipyard, Semakau — cells with lu_business_pct>=0.7 but bldg_industrial_count<5 and pc_cat_industrial_mfg<5 because the building-footprint feature does not cover reclaimed-island / offshore industrial estates. These are Singapore's MOST hazardous zones. Their downstream fire_risk_score, industrial_hazard_buffer, and nuisance_penalty (build_domain_primitives_sgp.py lines 116/121/131 all add minmax(lu_ind)+ind_adj) would UNDER-warn. Note lu_ind there partially rescues fire_risk/hazard via the +minmax(lu_ind) term, but the ind_adj contribution itself goes to 0. 66 of these 72 cells DO have max1_pc_cat_industrial_mfg>0 (neighbour-ring), so an existing-data rescue exists. The recipe's optional 'add est_total_floor_area / URA port flag' footnote is actually REQUIRED for these to score, not optional.

PROBLEM 3 — EMBEDDING LEAKAGE / STALE EMBEDDING (real side-effect, omitted). industrial_adjacency_score IS one of the 739 e1 embedding input columns (confirmed in embedding/meta.json; embedding/prep_features.py selects by exclusion and neither EXCLUDE_EXACT nor EXCLUDE_PREFIX excludes it). So (a) recomputing it and writing back to the master silently changes an e1 input and makes embedding/X.npy + Z_e1_s0/1/2.npy (built Jun 11) STALE unless prep_features.py and train.py are re-run; the recipe lists no embedding-rebuild step. (b) It is collinear with bldg_industrial_count and pc_cat_industrial_mfg, which are ALSO embedding inputs -> mild double-counting (pre-existing, but the fix re-strengthens that collinearity since corr to bldg rises to 0.70). Separately, the sibling nous_v4 fix's rent_retail_psf_est leaks via the rent_ -> PRICE view and vis_exit_footfall/retail_footfall_score also leak — these violate the 'rent/footfall must NOT be embedding inputs' constraint, but they are P0-1/P0-2, not P0-3. For P0-3 specifically: decide whether industrial_adjacency_score should be an e1 input at all (it is a derived guard signal redundant with two raw inputs) and either add it to EXCLUDE_EXACT or re-run prep+train.

PROBLEM 4 — NUMERIC / ACCEPTANCE-LITERAL MISMATCHES (minor). (a) lognorm divisor: log1p quantile of an all/near-zero column is 0; the formula's 'd if d>0 else 1' guard handles it, but res_penalty, the (bld-15)/35 and (poi-40)/120 clips, and own_presence/0.30 must keep their explicit clips or NaN/inf can appear — prototype was clean (no NaN/inf) only because every divisor was guarded. (b) Acceptance condition 3 literals are NOT reproducible on the live grid: recipe claims 'Jurong min 0.974' and 'Serangoon North Ind Estate 1.00', but I get JURONG min=0.324 (the bld=71,mfg=0 zero-POI Jurong cells) and SERANGOON NORTH IND min=0.000 (a low-building cell). These drops are arguably CORRECT (business-zoned but physically sparse), but the named-cell assertions as written will FAIL. Tuas min=0.680, Murai min=0.767, Kampong Ubi=1.000, Defu min=0.820 do pass >0.6.

What DID reproduce exactly: corr(new,bld)=0.704, corr(new,lu_biz)=0.528, corr(new,mfg)=0.524, ordering flip TRUE; Tiong Bahru new=0.0; heartland FP (>=5000 res,>=15 consumer POI,<10 ind bld, score>=0.5) 91(live)->9 (<=12 target met); FN bld>=40 = 0. So conditions 1, 2, 4(FP+FN40) pass; condition 3 partially fails on named literals; and the petrochemical regression is invisible to all 4 conditions.
result.corrected_recipe:
Keep the recipe's physical-anchor + own-presence-gated-ring + residential-dilution architecture (it correctly kills the heartland FP and never references lu_business_pct in the SCORE), but add a footprint-blind heavy-industry floor so petrochemical/island/wafer-fab zones are not zeroed, fix acceptance to compare against the LIVE column, and handle the embedding explicitly.

NEW BUILDER build_industrial_adjacency_sgp.py (run BEFORE build_domain_primitives_sgp.py; writes industrial_adjacency_score back into hex/hex8_all_features.parquet; back up first).

Inputs (all in master): hex8_id, bldg_industrial_count (bld), pc_cat_industrial_mfg (poi), pop_resident (res), lu_business_pct (lbp) — used ONLY for a hazard FLOOR, NOT in the score gradient, zone_type. h3 4.4.2 present.

helper lognorm(v,q=0.97): lv=log1p(clip(v,0,inf)); d=quantile(lv,q); d = d if d>0 else 1.0; return clip(lv/d,0,1)  # guarded divisor

Rings via h3.grid_disk (id->pos map): bld_k1,bld_k2,poi_k1,poi_k2 = ring SUMS over the 1191 cells.

own_bld=lognorm(bld); own_poi=lognorm(poi)
own=max(own_bld, 0.7*own_poi)
res_penalty=clip(1 - res/8000, 0, 1)
heavy=max(clip((bld-15)/35,0,1), clip((poi-40)/120,0,1))
own_eff=max(own*max(res_penalty,heavy), own_bld*heavy)
ring=max(lognorm((bld_k1-bld)+0.5*(bld_k2-bld_k1)), 0.8*lognorm((poi_k1-poi)+0.5*(poi_k2-poi_k1)))   # neighbours only
own_presence=clip(max(lognorm(bld,0.92),lognorm(poi,0.92))/0.30, 0, 1)
gated_ring=0.40*ring*own_presence*max(res_penalty,heavy)
base=max(own_eff, gated_ring)

# NEW — footprint-blind heavy-industry FLOOR (rescues Jurong Island/Bukom, Tuas View Ext, wafer-fab, shipyards).
# Fires ONLY in genuinely non-residential heavy-industry zones; uses lu_business_pct + neighbour-ring mfg as a FLOOR, never as a smear gradient, so heartland cells (which are residential and have res>0) are untouched.
heavy_zone = (zone_type in {industrial_empty,industrial_isolated,industrial_with_transit,islands_restricted}) AND (res < 200)
ring_mfg = lognorm(max1_pc_cat_industrial_mfg)   # existing col; >0 for 66/72 blind cells
hazard_floor = where(heavy_zone, clip(0.60*lbp + 0.40*ring_mfg, 0, 1)*0.85, 0.0)   # cap at 0.85 so observed-building cells still rank above pure-zoning cells
industrial_adjacency_score = round(clip(max(base, hazard_floor),0,1),4)

Notes: (1) buildings primary, POI 0.7; (2) lu_business_pct appears ONLY inside hazard_floor gated on non-residential heavy zones with res<200 — it cannot reach any residential heartland cell, so the FP fix is preserved; (3) ring smear neighbours-only, distance-decayed, own-presence gated; (4) residential dilution kills light-workshop noise; (5) every divisor guarded -> no NaN/inf.

EMBEDDING handling (mandatory, was missing): EITHER (preferred) add "industrial_adjacency_score" to EXCLUDE_EXACT in embedding/prep_features.py (it is a derived guard redundant with bldg_industrial_count + pc_cat_industrial_mfg which are already inputs) so it stops leaking and is not double-counted; OR if it must stay an e1 input, re-run embedding/prep_features.py then embedding/train.py to regenerate X.npy + Z_e1_s0/1/2.npy (currently Jun 11, will be stale). Do NOT leave the recomputed column in the master while the embedding npz is stale. (Flag separately to the orchestrator: rent_retail_psf_est, vis_exit_footfall, retail_footfall_score from the sibling P0-1/P0-2 fixes also currently leak into e1 via the rent_ PRICE view and the score sweep — same decision needed there, out of P0-3 scope.)

DOWNSTREAM: after writing, re-run build_domain_primitives_sgp.py so fire_risk_score, industrial_hazard_buffer, nuisance_penalty inherit the corrected ind_adj (they read minmax(industrial_adjacency_score)). Back up the master first.
result.final_acceptance:
Run on the recomputed column over hex8 (n=1191). Baselines are the LIVE column (post nous_v4: corr_bld=0.552, corr_lu_biz=0.371, FP91, FN_bld25=0), NOT the stale pre-fix snapshot.

1. ORDERING / DECOUPLING: corr(new, bldg_industrial_count) > corr(new, lu_business_pct) AND corr(new, pc_cat_industrial_mfg) >= 0.50. Prototype: 0.704 vs ~0.53, mfg 0.524. PASS expected (hazard_floor adds a small lu_business component to 72 cells, so allow corr(new,lu_business_pct) to land up to ~0.58; the strict requirement is corr_bld > corr_lu_biz, which holds at 0.70 vs <=0.58).

2. HEARTLAND FP <= 12: cells with pop_resident>=5000 AND consumer_POI(sum pc_cat_* minus industrial_mfg)>=15 AND bldg_industrial_count<10 AND score>=0.5. Prototype 9. Assert <=12. Also Tiong Bahru max score < 0.05 (prototype 0.0) and no cell with pop_resident>=5000 & bldg_industrial_count<10 scores >=0.5 from ring smear alone.

3. PHYS-INDUSTRIAL >0.6: Tuas min, Murai, Kampong Ubi, Defu cells (bldg>=10) all >0.6 (prototype Tuas 0.680 / Murai 0.767 / Kampong Ubi 1.0 / Defu 0.820). DROP the literal 'Jurong 0.974 / Serangoon 1.00' assertions — they are not reproducible and the drops are correct; instead assert Jurong/Serangoon cells WITH bldg_industrial_count>=25 score >0.6.

4. NEW — PETROCHEMICAL / FOOTPRINT-BLIND FLOOR: every cell with lu_business_pct>=0.7 AND zone_type in {industrial_empty,industrial_isolated,industrial_with_transit,islands_restricted} AND pop_resident<200 scores >= 0.40 (target the 72-cell set; without the floor these are ~0). Spot-check JURONG ISLAND AND BUKOM, TUAS VIEW EXTENSION, PASIR RIS WAFER FAB PARK > 0.40.

5. NO REGRESSION ON FN vs LIVE: FN bld>=40 = 0 (prototype 0); FN bld>=25 <= 6 (prototype 5 — accept the small heartland-embedded light-industry tradeoff: Bendemeer/Taman Jurong/Potong Pasir).

6. STABILITY: 0 NaN, 0 inf, all values in [0,1], n=1191 unchanged.

7. EMBEDDING CONSISTENCY: either industrial_adjacency_score is absent from embedding/meta.json cols (added to EXCLUDE_EXACT), OR embedding/X.npy and Z_e1_s{0,1,2}.npy mtime is newer than the master rewrite (re-trained). Assert one of the two.

8. DOWNSTREAM: build_domain_primitives_sgp.py re-run; fire_risk_score / industrial_hazard_buffer / nuisance_penalty regenerated with no new NaN and non-zero on the 72 petrochemical cells.

Re-run the original nous P0-3 queries after rebuild; confirm 1-6 and spot-check the named cells plus Jurong Island.

result.problems:
The diagnosis and the core direction (split transport into terminal/transit via lu_transport_pct>=0.8; deterministically fill the 247 unknowns; reclass Sentosa) are sound and all nous evidence reproduces exactly on /home/azureuser/da-sgp/v5/. But the recipe as written FAILS its own acceptance check and breaks two existing consumers. Verified problems:

1) WRONG ACCEPTANCE NUMBER (islands_restricted). Recipe claims islands_restricted=259. Live simulation of STEP B+C gives 255. Arithmetic: 148 current + 111 filled (WESTERN ISLANDS 60 + NORTH-EASTERN ISLANDS 39 + SOUTHERN-ISLANDS-non-Sentosa 12) = 259, but STEP C then reclassifies the 4 currently-islands_restricted Sentosa cells to islands_resort, so 259-4 = 255. The recipe double-counts; the correct target is 255.

2) hex9 HAS NO zone_type COLUMN (fatal for acceptance check 4 and the STEP claim). hex9_all_features.parquet (7318x597) contains NO 'zone_type' and NO 'zone_type_broad' column (only dominant_use + lu_transport_pct). There is no existing hex9 'inheritance step that copies hex8 zone columns down' to re-run. Acceptance check (4) 'hex9 zone_type unknown count==0' tests a column that does not exist and would KeyError. transport_subtype CAN be derived on hex9 (730 transport cells: 443 terminal / 287 transit) but only by adding it fresh, not by 're-inheriting'.

3) zone_type_broad NOT RE-DERIVED (breaks the actual NA-mask consumer). The mobility/adequacy NA-mask reads zone_type_broad, NOT zone_type (build_mobility_pack.py L164-169: NA_ZONES={industrial,airport,nature,islands,future}; na_mask=zone_type_broad.isin(NA_ZONES)). zone_type_broad has its own 247 'unknown' that mirror zone_type=='unknown'. The recipe says 're-derive zone_type_broad if present' but never specifies the mapping, and the two NEW zone_type values it introduces (institutional_isolated, transport_terminal) have NO existing broad mapping -> zone_type_broad coverage drops below 1.0 -> validate_mobility_pack.py M4 (requires zt_cov==1.0) FAILS. This is a hard break of an existing validator.

4) STEP C IS SELF-DEFEATING for its stated goal. Setting Sentosa to islands_resort maps to zone_type_broad='islands', which IS in NA_ZONES, so cell 463 (Resorts World retail core, retail_footfall_score=50, vis_exit_footfall=14721) gets NA-masked and its adq fields set NaN -> the exact opposite of 'makes the existing footfall eligible for scoring.' Note: footfall/retail columns themselves are NOT adq fields, so they are never masked and remain populated for any direct consumer; but the mobility ADEQUACY score (the thing the recipe wants) will exclude Sentosa as long as it is 'islands'. To make Sentosa scoreable you must give islands_resort a broad value NOT in NA_ZONES (decision required and not stated).

5) UNSTATED SIDE-EFFECT (correct, but must be acknowledged + validated). Filling the 247 unknowns moves ~221 cells that were previously NOT NA-masked (unknown is not in NA_ZONES) into NA broad classes (islands/nature/airport/industrial), so their adq fields become NaN. old NA=497 -> new NA=718. This is the desired P1-1 behavior (Jurong Island/Tuas interiors, restricted islands, airside should be Not-Applicable) but the acceptance check never checks it; M4's 'non-res hexes adq==NaN' must be re-asserted.

6) REDUNDANCY (harmless): STEP B rule 1 (Sentosa->islands_resort) is fully overridden by STEP C (all Sentosa->islands_resort), so it is dead logic; fine to drop.

7) NOT A PROBLEM, confirmed clean: (a) No embedding leakage. transport_subtype is an object/string column -> dropped by select_dtypes(number) in embedding/prep_features.py; zone_type is already excluded by EXCLUDE_PREFIX; this fix adds no rent/footfall to X. (b) Numerically stable: lu_transport_pct, lu_business_pct in [0,1] with 0 NaN, dominant_use/parent_pa/parent_subzone_name 0 NaN on both grids -> no winsorization/zero/NaN handling needed. Separability reproduced: terminal spend==0 frac 0.657, transit spend>0 frac 0.667; terminal iso_walk10_pop median 0, transit median 90.675.
result.corrected_recipe:
Implement as a post-fold patch script (pattern of patch_rent_v57.py) operating on hex8 master, then RE-DERIVE zone_type_broad, then ADD (not re-inherit) the new columns to hex9. Decide upfront: Sentosa/islands_resort policy (Option A recommended).

STEP A - transport_subtype (hex8 + hex9, derived independently per grain, NOT inherited):
For each grain df (use its own dominant_use + lu_transport_pct, both NaN-free):
  transport_subtype = 'not_transport' where dominant_use!='transport'
  else 'transport_terminal' where lu_transport_pct>=0.8
  else 'transport_transit'.
hex8 yields {not_transport:1073, transport_terminal:70, transport_transit:48}. hex9 yields {transport_terminal:443, transport_transit:287, not_transport:6588}. String dtype (auto-excluded from embeddings).

STEP B - deterministic fill of the 247 hex8 unknowns (apply ONLY to zone_type=='unknown', priority order; drop the redundant Sentosa rule since STEP C overrides it):
  1) parent_pa in {WESTERN ISLANDS, NORTH-EASTERN ISLANDS, SOUTHERN ISLANDS} -> 'islands_restricted'
  2) elif parent_pa in {CHANGI, CHANGI BAY} -> 'airport_operations'
  3) elif dominant_use=='transport' and lu_transport_pct>=0.8 -> 'industrial_isolated' (do NOT introduce a new 'transport_terminal' zone_type value; transport detail already lives in transport_subtype + zone_type_broad would be orphaned. These 22 airside interiors are non-leasable and belong in an NA class; 'industrial_isolated'->broad 'industrial' is NA, which is correct)
  4) elif dominant_use in {business, commercial} and lu_business_pct>=0.5 -> 'industrial_isolated'
  5) elif dominant_use in {reserve, open_space, water, utility} -> 'nature'
  6) elif dominant_use=='institutional' -> 'nature' (map institutional islands/reserves into an EXISTING NA-capable broad; do NOT invent 'institutional_isolated' which has no zone_type_broad mapping and would fail M4. If a distinct label is wanted, you MUST also add it to broad_map below with an explicit broad value)
  7) elif dominant_use=='residential' -> 'residential'
  8) else -> 'industrial_isolated'

result.problems:
The recipe's spine is correct and the headline evidence reproduces exactly (hex8 (1191,846), hex9 (7318,597), 262 cols absent, parent_hex8 present, all named families 100% absent from hex9; native hex9 inputs all exist: places carry hex9_id, hex9_universe has lat/lng, hex9_population has pop_resident+parent_pa). But several specific claims are WRONG and two acceptance gates would FAIL as written.

1) MIS-SCOPED NATIVE SET — min15_* and industrial_adjacency_score are NOT recomputable from v5 data. They are not produced by any v5 builder. build_mobility_pack.py (S11) only TAKES them from an external file: /home/azureuser/sgp-mobility-v2/dist/data/hex8_adequacy.geojson (a separate hex8-only adequacy app). There is no hex9 source and no v5-local formula. So min15_* (10 cols) and industrial_adjacency_score belong in INHERIT, not NATIVE-RECOMPUTE, unless the upstream sgp-mobility-v2 pipeline is ported (external work, not proven from atlas data). zone_type/zone_type_broad/mrt_reach_*/time_to_*/adq_* come from the same geojson — recipe already inherits most of these, good, but it wrongly groups min15/industrial with the natives.

2) ca_footfall AND commercial_activity_index ARE NOT NATIVE — build_commercial_activity_hex8.py: ca_footfall = minmax(od_throughput) (OD-structural, hex8-only by the recipe's own OD argument). commercial_activity_index = mean(ca_nl, ca_spend, ca_taps, ca_places, ca_footfall); ca_taps = daily_bus_taps + daily_train_taps (transit-grain), ca_footfall = od_throughput. So the index is a HYBRID: nl/spend/places are point/raster-grain (native at hex9), but taps/footfall are hex8-structural. Listing ca_footfall and commercial_activity_index as native-changed columns is incorrect — ca_footfall must inherit; the index must be marked hybrid (native parts recomputed, taps/footfall inherited from parent_hex8) or inherited wholesale.

3) SEVERANCE GATE MIS-CALIBRATED — gate (3) demands median hex9 iso_severance_ratio in 0.35-0.65. The builder docstring's '~0.55 ideal grid' is aspirational; the ACTUAL measured hex8 median (iso_walk_report.json) is 0.219. The gate would fail even on hex8's own distribution. Must re-anchor to ~0.22 (parity-with-hex8), not 0.55.

4) CHILD-COUNT / SIBLING-GROUP ASSUMPTION WRONG — gates (1) and (6) assume '7 hex9 children of each populated hex8'. Mean children per hex8 is 6.14 (boundary clipping), and median POPULATED siblings per parent is 1.0; only 591 parents have >=2 populated children and 427 have all 7 populated. A within-parent CV over all sibling groups is undefined/0 for singleton-populated parents and would drag the median. Gate must restrict to parents with >=2 populated children. (Verified by prototype: over those 591 parents, median within-parent CV of catchment pop = 0.224 and 81.2% exceed CV>0.10 — so the de-smearing gate PASSES once the denominator is fixed.)

5) VISIBILITY SUB-CLAIM IMPRECISE — only vis_exit_footfall (and vis_dist_exit_origin_m) are origin-keyed in build_visibility.py. vis_main_road_m / vis_traffic_pass_proxy / vis_corner_premium are computed by binning LTA speed-band segment midpoints via h3.latlng_to_cell(..., 8) — the fix is to RE-BIN at res 9 (valid: segment geometry is point-grain), not 'swap the origin'. vis_corner_premium also reads sig*count from the master — at hex9 it must read the hex9 master's signal-count column. min15_nearest_super_m etc. cannot be recomputed at all (see #1).

6) NO NEW LEAKAGE, BUT CONFIRM A PRE-EXISTING ONE IS NOT WIDENED — the user's worry 'rent/footfall must not be embedding inputs' is ALREADY the case in the hex8 design: embedding/prep_features.py INCLUDES iso_*, vis_*, ca_*, commercial_activity, rent_*, nl_*, min15_* as FLOW/PRICE/WHO inputs and only EXCLUDES od_throughput, hdb_resale_4r_median_psm, adq_default and the OPPORTUNITY view. Crucially e1/p1 are HEX8-ONLY (read hex8_all_features). The recipe is hex9-output-only, so it introduces NO new leakage into e1/p1 — PROVIDED it (a) never writes to hex8_all_features, (b) does not trigger an embedding rebuild, and (c) if a hex9 embedding is ever built later, it inherits the same EXCLUDE contract (must NOT add od_throughput natively — verified od_throughput is currently absent from hex9; keep it absent or in the exclude set).

7) NUMERICAL STABILITY — pack builders use minmax() on GLOBAL 1st/99th percentile. Re-running them on a hex9 master re-fits normalization to the hex9 distribution: scores become intra-hex9-relative and are NOT comparable to the hex8 score of the same name (a hex9 footfall_score=0.8 != hex8 0.8). This is acceptable for within-hex9 ranking but MUST be documented (and the catalog granularity tag must flag the re-fit), else downstream cross-grain comparisons silently break. iso_severance_ratio is already guarded (NaN where euclid_pop<200) — keep that. Watch division by zero in min15/severance and winsorize iso_walk10_pop tail (mean 2577 vs median 2.6 — extreme right skew) before any minmax.

No collinearity problem with the thing being replaced: today hex9 carries the SMEARED parent value (constant within parent), so native de-smearing strictly ADDS within-parent variance — it cannot be collinear with a constant. No double-counting as long as inherited od/dt/transit families are NOT also re-derived natively.
